note: Everything the keyboard is, in one place. The firmware's constants are generated from this by tools/generate_keyboards.py, and LEVEL's layout page reads this very file, so nothing here is ever copied anywhere by hand.

geometry.note: In millimetres, so that a key stays the same size under a finger on a panel of any density: a sharper screen draws the same key with more points, not a smaller key. A key that writes is a little wider than it is tall, because a row of them is read across and a finger travels sideways between them more often than up. The keyboard keeps a margin tighter than the screen's, because a key at the edge is still a key and its row has to reach the glass. What stands on a key is stated as the height of a capital rather than as a point size, since the capital is the part one sees and the point size is the figure a typeface wants for it. A control says what it does in a corner, so the middle of a row stays clear and the eye reads across it.
geometry.grid: The figures are the millimetre that lands on the point wanted rather than the round one. This panel puts 7.35 points on a millimetre, so 1.5 mm comes out at 11 points and every key after it sits half a pixel off the grid. A panel rounds, and the layout page reports a value that lands between two points instead of quietly moving it.

colours.note: The three surfaces a key can be, what a key says, and the two quiet marks.

type.note: The cut the keys are set in. The point size is not stated: it follows from the cap heights above and the typeface's cap ratio, and LEVEL's tools/fonts.sh works it out rather than being told.

extras.note: The characters a symbol row may hold, in the order they are laid out, grouped so that a row of the keyboard means something. A layout takes from each group only what its own letters cannot reach, which is why a country with a fuller keyboard shows fewer symbols.

layouts.note: Each country's first layer entire. `rows` is what the keys say unshifted and `shifted` is what shift makes of each of them, position by position, with a space where it makes nothing new. `symbols` is derived rather than decided: the generator works it out and writes it back here, so editing it by hand is undone at the next build.

german.note: German ISO, its first layer entire: the circumflex left of the 1, the sharp s right of the 0, and the + and the # at the trailing ends.

english.note: US layout, its first layer entire, down to the backslash right of the apostrophe.

french.note: AZERTY, and the one layout whose digits come with shift rather than without. That is kept: the accents stand unshifted where they do on the keyboard, and the digits over them.

spanish.note: Spanish ISO, its first layer entire, with the n with a tilde and the c with a cedilla right of the l.

italian.note: Italian ISO, its first layer entire, with the e with a grave right of the p and the o, a and u with graves right of the l.
